title: Deep Sea Bottle Fishing Challenge
description: The player controls a glowing water bottle submarine descending through an underwater scene to catch elusive barramundi fish. Fish swim in randomized patrol patterns at varying depths, and the player must maneuver the bottle to align and capture each fish by pressing a key when close enough. A scoring system tracks catches, misses, and a countdown timer adds pressure.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an underwater fishing mini-game. Load BarramundiFish.glb and WaterBottle.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: use a dark blue-to-black gradient background (fog and scene.background color #001030). Add subtle ambient light (intensity 0.3, blue tint) and a point light attached to the bottle (aqua color, intensity 2, distance 15) to simulate a submarine headlight. Camera: use a third-person perspective camera that follows the bottle from behind and slightly above. The WaterBottle model acts as the player's submarine. Scale it to roughly 1.5x and orient it horizontally. The player moves it with WASD keys for horizontal movement and Q/E for ascending/descending. Clamp movement within a bounding box of 20x12x20 units. Spawn 5 BarramundiFish instances at random positions within the play area. Each fish should have a unique sinusoidal patrol path, oscillating on the X and Z axes with randomized amplitude and frequency, and gently bobbing on Y. Fish should rotate to face their movement direction. Implement a capture mechanic: when the bottle is within 2 units of a fish and the player presses SPACE, check alignment (bottle must face within 30 degrees of the fish direction). On success, the fish plays a scale-down animation and disappears, score increments. On failure (too far or bad angle), flash the screen border red briefly and increment a miss counter. Add a 60-second countdown timer displayed as an HTML overlay. Display current score, misses, and time remaining. When all 5 fish are caught, show a victory message with total time and accuracy percentage. When time expires, show game-over with fish remaining. Add floating particle sprites (small blue-white dots) drifting upward slowly to simulate underwater bubbles. Validate that score never exceeds fish count and misses are tracked accurately. Ensure all parameters (distance threshold, angle threshold, timer, fish count) are defined as named constants at the top of the script for easy tuning.
